notes: §1985:VI.6.23.3 SR3: "Identifier-3 must reference an elementary numeric integer." BindSetUpDown binds the UP BY/DOWN BY amount under OperandContext.ArithmeticIndexWindow, whose 2023 row (§2023:13.18.38.3 r7, §2023:13.18.60.3 SR10) admits an index-name and an index data item, and the 85 gate GateCobol85IndexAmount/IsCobol85IndexAmount refuses only a scaled numeric item, a non-integer literal or an expression; nothing at 85 refuses an index-name or a USAGE INDEX item as identifier-3. Refused at 85: PIC 9V9 (the witness), SVPP9, N + 1, a function (COBOL0900), alphanumeric, numeric-edited, group, reference-modified (COBOL0844), an unsubscripted table element (COBOL2270). Accepted wrongly: SET IX UP BY IDX (USAGE INDEX) and SET IX UP BY IY / DOWN BY JX (index-names), each compiling and moving IX by the other index's occurrence number. Accepted rightly: 99, S9(4), COMP, COMP-3, 9(18), 9PP, a subscripted integer. kb/Work PB5421 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read3/rd-01.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Identifier-3 must reference an elementary numeric integer."; 2023: "No syntax rule of 14.9.39.3 constrains the UP BY/DOWN BY operand; the 2023 identifier-3 is an object-class receiving item.". The 2023 SET syntax rules shown never limit the UP BY/DOWN BY operand to an elementary numeric integer. The name identifier-3 now denotes an object reference, so the restriction is gone.
